title: Multi-Year Subscription Cutover & Close-the-Loop: Contract-to-Cash Playbook
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Overview

This playbook defines the operational, accounting, and product steps required for a cutover from legacy single‑year subscription billing to multi‑year subscription contracts (MYSC). It covers forecasting implications, contract validation, procurement handoffs, billing configuration, revenue deferral/recognition rules, and escalation paths to ensure clean month/quarter close and minimize revenue leakage.

Scope

- Applies to all customer contracts with term > 12 months, including renewals that change term length to multi‑year.
- Affects Sales (offer creation & contracting), Legal (clause review), RevOps/Billing (billing config and invoice delivery), Finance (revrec, AR, forecasts), and Product/Platform (metering & usage tagging).
- Excludes one‑off professional services that are separately invoiced and recognized.

Definitions

- MYSC: Multi‑Year Subscription Contract (term > 12 months).
- Billing Cutover: The operational window during which Billing system configuration is updated and invoices are issued under the new model.
- Deferred Revenue Bucket: GL account holding unrecognized subscription revenue.

Goals & Acceptance Criteria

- No lost or duplicated invoices for cutover cohort.
- Revenue recognition aligns with ASC 606 / IFRS 15 principles and internal policy: deferred then recognized pro rata unless a contract specifies milestone-based recognition.
- Forecast accuracy for the first two post‑cutover quarters within ±3% of actual recognized revenue for affected accounts.
- Contract-to-billing SLA: Sales -> RevOps handoff validated in <= 2 business days.

Owners & Contacts

- Playbook owner: Ava Martinez (Finance Ops) — ava.martinez@redwood.ai
- Billing configuration lead: Marcus Patel (RevOps) — marcus.patel@redwood.ai
- Revenue recognition lead: Eleanor Wu (Accounting) — eleanor.wu@redwood.ai
- Legal reviewer: Diego Ramirez (Legal) — diego.ramirez@redwood.ai
- Escalation: Finance Director (oncall) — finance-oncall@redwood.ai

High-Level Cutover Phases

1) Pre-Cutover Validation (T-30 to T-7 days)
   - Identify affected contracts via contract lifecycle system (CLS) filter: term > 12 months OR renewal flagged "multi-year".
   - Run automated contract parser to extract: start_date, term_months, bill_cycle_anchor, currency, payment_terms, revenue_allocation_rules.
   - Manual review queue for contracts with non-standard clauses (discount ladders, price escalators, milestone recognition).
   - Confirm mapping to product SKUs and accounting codes (see GL Mapping table below).

2) Billing Configuration & Staging (T-14 to T-3 days)
   - Create staging invoices in the Billing API sandbox for a representative sample of 50 accounts (small / medium / large MRR buckets).
   - Verify invoice payloads match accounting allocation: invoice_total, deferred_amount, immediate_recognition_amount.
   - Validate purchase order (PO) and tax handling for multi-year prepay scenarios.

3) Cutover Execution (T-1 to T+2 days)
   - Freeze changes to contracts for cutover cohort at T-1 18:00 local.
   - Apply billing config to production during nightly maintenance window (22:00–02:00 PT).
   - Issue invoices per normal cadence. For annual prepay multi-year deals, create single invoice and set deferral schedule in AR system.
   - Run end-to-end test: invoice -> payment gateway -> cash application -> deferred revenue entry.

4) Post-Cutover Reconciliation (T+3 to T+14 days)
   - Reconcile staged sample: match invoice numbers, payment status, and GL entries.
   - Run revenue recognition sanity checks: monthly recognized revenue equals scheduled deferral amortization.
   - Adjust forecast models for bookings to reflect multi‑year ARR/ACV treatment.

Contract Validation Checklist (pre-cutover)

- Contract signed and countersigned with electronic signature.
- Term start date and end date explicitly defined.
- Payment term: prepay/annual/quarterly/monthly specified.
- Cancellation and refund policy clearly specified.
- Pricing escalation clauses flagged and documented.
- PO number collected when required by customer.

GL Mapping and Accounting Config (table)

| Product SKU | Revenue GL Account | Deferred Revenue GL | Recognition Rule |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| API-STD | 4001-SaaS-Revenue | 2102-Deferred-Sub | Straight-line monthly over term |
| API-PRO | 4002-SaaS-Revenue | 2102-Deferred-Sub | Immediate recognition of onboarding fee; remainder straight-line |
| DEDICATED-POOL | 4005-Dedicated | 2105-Deferred-Ded | Recognize per usage report monthly |

Revenue Recognition Rules (detailed)

- Default rule for MYSC: recognize subscription revenue pro rata monthly over the committed term starting from service activation date.
- Prepayment: when cash received in advance, book to Deferred Revenue GL and amortize monthly.
- Discounts: allocate discount across performance obligations using relative standalone selling price; reflect in deferred schedule.
- Termination with refund clause: revenue recognized up to termination date; remaining deferred revenue reversed and classified as customer refund liability until settled.

Sample Invoice JSON (billing API payload)

{
  "customer_id": "cust_12345",
  "currency": "USD",
  "invoice_date": "2026-03-01",
  "items": [
    {"sku": "API-PRO", "quantity": 1, "unit_price": 120000, "billing_period_months": 36 }
  ],
  "total_amount": 120000,
  "allocation": {"immediate_recognition": 0, "deferred_amount": 120000}
}

Operational SLAs

- Sales -> RevOps contract handoff: 2 business days to validate metadata.
- Billing config deployment: <= 1 maintenance window during cutover night.
- Reconciliation of sample cohort: complete within 10 business days post-cutover.
- Exception resolution (nonstandard contract): 5 business days for Legal + Finance review.

Forecasting & Modeling Notes

- Bookings vs Recognized: For multi‑year deals the initial booking will show full booking value in bookings metrics but only monthly recognized revenue contributes to ARR/recognized revenue forecasts.
- Model change: Add a deferred revenue layer and a subscription amortization schedule to the quarterly forecast model (see Forecast Workbook tab "MYSC Amortization").
- Sensitivity: Run upside/downside scenarios with 0%, 5%, and 15% early churn rates affecting recognized revenue in first 24 months.

Procurement & Payment Terms Implications

- For customers requiring PO-based procurement, ensure PO is attached to the CLS entry prior to invoice generation.
- Prepay discounts must be codified in contract and mirrored in billing itemization.
- For enterprise customers with milestone payments, coordinate milestone invoices with Product Delivery and Legal sign-off.

Exception Handling & Rollback Plan

1) If >2% of cutover invoices fail to generate or are materially incorrect: trigger rollback to previous invoicing model for affected accounts and open a Severity 2 incident.
2) Rollback steps: disable cutover toggle, re-run legacy invoice generator for failed accounts, notify customers, and create corrective invoices.
3) Post-mortem: 3 business days to produce incident summary and remediation plan, with owners assigned.

Escalation Matrix

- Level 1 (Billing): Marcus Patel — revops-billing@redwood.ai (first 2 business hours)
- Level 2 (Revenue Ops / Finance): Ava Martinez & Eleanor Wu — finance-ops@redwood.ai (within 4 business hours)
- Level 3 (Legal / Executive): Diego Ramirez & Head of Finance — legal-finance-escalation@redwood.ai (within 8 business hours)

Monitoring & Post-Cutover Alerts

- Create dashboard: "MYSC Cutover — Invoice Success Rate" (target >= 99.5%).
- Create alert: invoice_failure_rate > 0.5% for >1 hour -> page oncall Finance.
- Daily reconciliation job: compare Billing API invoice exports to GL entries; discrepancy > $5,000 triggers manual review.

Retention of Evidence & Audit Trail

- Attach final signed contracts, invoice PDFs, payment receipts, and journal entries to CLS contract record.
- Maintain reconciliations and cutover runbooks for 7 years for audit purposes.

Appendix A — Journal Entry Examples

1) Annual prepay invoice (single invoice for 36 months, $120,000):
   - DR Cash 120,000
   - CR Deferred Revenue 120,000

2) Monthly recognition entry (monthly amortization $3,333.33):
   - DR Deferred Revenue 3,333.33
   - CR SaaS Revenue 3,333.33

Appendix B — Quick CLI commands (examples)

- Export contract cohort: 
  `./scripts/export_contracts.sh --term-min 12 --status signed --output mysc-cohort.csv`
- Generate staging invoices: 
  `billingctl create-batch --env staging --file mysc-sample.json`
